lines.text: Hi, I'm Sindy! Let's get onto the nodes of your cluster.
Your cluster is up, but its nodes are containers. How do you get a shell on one, or run a quick command there?
Say you're testing a job script, and want to look around on a worker. sind gives you three ways in: ssh, enter and exec.
sind ssh logs you in to any node by its name, here the controller.
To run a command on a node, put it after two dashes. Full-screen programs like top also want the t flag.
Under the hood, sind ssh runs ssh in a relay container on the mesh, which reaches every node by name.
sind enter opens a shell on the submitter, or on the controller if there's none, right in the data directory.
sind exec runs a single command there instead, and passes back its exit status, here three.
That data directory is your current directory on the host, mounted on every node.
sind ssh starts in your home directory instead, so change into the data directory there.
And to use your own ssh client, include the SSH config that sind exports for each realm.
So: sind ssh reaches any node by name, enter and exec land in the data directory, and your own client needs one include line.
Next up: adding and removing workers. See you there!
